changes.before: Success would support numerical reproduction for that chosen reconstruction. It would not uniquely establish historical inputs, validate the other eight groups, or establish prospective physical accuracy. Extend the check to all nine groups before attaching ensemble resource estimates. Failure blocks attaching the present conditional calculations to the historical predictor; it does not exclude every admissible mapping or quantum method.
changes.after: Success at this criterion would establish an aggregate-output reproduction milestone for that chosen reconstruction. Agreement of the five-model group means, even for all nine groups, does not validate individual-model outputs or latent norm products: discrepancies between members can compensate in a mean. Retaining activations and norm products records the reconstruction but does not itself validate them. The aggregate check must therefore be distinguished from the additional input and per-model validation needed before resource estimates can be attached to the released predictor. Extend the aggregate check to all nine groups, while keeping that validation gap explicit. Neither aggregate agreement nor this extension uniquely establishes historical inputs or prospective physical accuracy. Failure blocks attaching the present conditional calculations to the historical predictor; it does not exclude every admissible mapping or quantum method.

findings.quote: State beside the reproduction criterion that agreement of group means, including all nine groups, does not validate individual-model outputs or latent norm products. Distinguish the proposed aggregate-output reproduction milestone from the additional input and per-model validation needed to attach resource estimates to the released predictor; do not imply that passing the aggregate criterion alone closes that gap.
